title: AuthN Onboarding + Least-Privilege Design Review — Marigold Health

Agreed next steps: share SOC 2 and network diagrams, produce a SCIM role mapping example, and schedule a separate POC benchmarking session for SAML assertion throughput.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-10 16:00 PST
Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sasha (Redwood SE), Anita (Marigold Head Security), Priya (IAM), Liam (Platform), Diego (DevOps)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): Quick security deep dive. Main asks: SOC2, SCIM mapping, SAML metadata, KMS integration.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. we have Sasha from our solutions team too. how's everyone doing?
00:08 Anita: Good thanks, running a bit tight but ready. we've been evaluating a few inference vendors and i'd like to walk through our SSO requirements and the least-privilege model.
00:16 Sasha: Great, quick agenda — SAML exchange, SCIM provisioning, role mapping for least privilege, and our encryption/KMS patterns. i'll call out what we recommend for hosted vs private deployments.
00:29 Liam: One quick note — Marigold needs EU-only residency for a subset of patient data. want to confirm how Redwood handles region pinning and audit logs.
00:38 Jordan: Absolutely. at a high level we support hosted API with region selection, Dedicated and Private deployments in a VPC. for EU residency we can run Private in eu-west region, that's common.
00:50 Priya: On SCIM, we want group sync to map to entitlements. can we do delta syncs and stop user provisioning from creating accounts we don't want?
01:01 Sasha: Yes, SCIM group sync is configurable. most customers use group slicing — map a SCIM group to a Redwood role. you can set provisioning to create users only, or just sync groups. note: the default is create+update, but we can change that per tenant.
01:18 Diego: Any gotchas on SCIM attributes? we use custom attributes like marigold:site and environment tags.
01:26 Sasha: custom attrs are fine but SCIM attribute mapping is case-sensitive on some IdPs; sometimes the IdP names come through slightly different. also our SCIM endpoints expect standard urn:ietf attributes for email, displayName — extra attrs go into profile metadata, they don't always map to RBAC rules automatically.
01:44 Anita: SAML assertions — we need to assert groups in the AAD token and also have signed assertions via our HSM. are there latency or throughput implications?
01:54 Sasha: SAML itself shouldn't create throughput issues unless you're spamming logins. for provisioning and token exchange we recommend caching the last-known groups for 15 minutes to avoid repeated IdP calls. prefix/KV cache in the runtime reduces per-call latency, that's our inference cache not the auth cache, but we do have auth caching layers.
02:15 Jordan: Regarding signed assertions and private keys — customers can host keys in their KMS/HSM and Redwood supports SP-initiated SAML with IdP metadata. we can also support signed SAML using customer's public cert.
02:28 Priya: How does key management work for model data and logs? we need envelope encryption and control of key rotation.
02:35 Sasha: For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSM). envelope encryption is standard: we encrypt data keys with customer KMS. for hosted customers we can offer BYOK (bring-your-own-key) via a customer-managed KMS grant where possible. note: BYOK for hosted is limited for certain cloud regions and may require enterprise contract.
03:02 Liam: Audit logs — what granularity and retention? we need admin-level audit trail for SSO events, provisioning, and model access.
03:12 Jordan: Audit logs include SAML auth events, SCIM provisioning events (create/update/delete), role changes, and API token usage. retention defaults to 90 days in standard plan; enterprise can extend to 7 years in our logs add-on. logs can be exported to your log sinks (S3/Blob) or forwarded to SIEM via webhook.
03:35 Anita: Is the audit stream tamper-evident? we need integrity assurances for compliance.
03:41 Sasha: We can provide signed log bundles for Private deployments and append-only storage for enterprise customers. hosted logs are write-once in our secure store and we support pushing to a customer-controlled storage account if you require more rigorous controls.
03:58 Diego: For RBAC, we want least-privilege by default. our current pattern: infra-admins, app-ops, data-ops, analyst-readonly. want to see recommended role slicing.
04:10 Sasha: Recommended approach: start with tenant-level roles (owner, admin, operator, readonly), then slice by function. use SCIM groups for entitlements and keep user roles minimal. avoid mapping broad groups like "All Engineers" to admin. use just-in-time elevation patterns for break-glass.
04:30 Priya: Can we do time-bound roles? e.g., grant admin for 4 hours for a change window.
04:36 Jordan: We support temporary role grants via our Console APIs; you can set TTL on role assignments or integrate with your JIT provider.
04:45 Anita: For SAML metadata exchange, what's the typical artifact you need from us?
04:50 Sasha: We need IdP metadata (XML) or SAML endpoints, signing cert, and attribute mappings. we'll produce SP metadata for you to import. we'll also give a sample assertion for testing.
05:02 Liam: Any network concerns for Private vs Hosted? egress/VPC peering?
05:08 Sasha: Private deployment sits inside your VPC with private subnets and security groups. for hosted we do TLS over public endpoints with IP allowlisting and egress rules. dedicated pools can be provisioned in a customer VPC via interconnect/peering, typical pattern for low-latency.
05:25 Anita: SOC 2 and ISO — can you share your attestation and scope?
05:30 Jordan: Yes, we'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO scope doc. SOC 2 covers our control plane and hosted service; Private deployments have separate attestations depending on the customer contract.
05:45 Diego: Any limitations on SCIM batch size? we have 20k users across orgs.
05:51 Sasha: SCIM endpoints support paging and delta sync. for large orgs we recommend incremental syncs and setting a backoff. performance is fine but we'll run a throughput POC to validate.
06:05 Priya: Can we map multiple IdP groups into a single Redwood role? for example map eng-sre + eng-oncall -> operator.
06:12 Sasha: Yes, SCIM group mappings can be one-to-many. our mapping UI supports pattern matching for group names and regex mapping.
06:23 Anita: Ok let's talk about a concrete mapping — we'll share our groups.
06:28 Jordan: Great, next steps: Sasha will put together a mapping example and sample metadata. i will send SOC2 and network diagram. we should schedule a 30-minute POC for SAML throughput and a 1-hour follow-up to finalize RBAC slices.
06:42 Liam: timeline wise, we're targeting an in-production pilot in Q1 end. need to line up procurement and security signoff.
06:49 Jordan: Sounds good, we'll aim to get docs to you this week.
06:55 Anita: quick question — for audit log exports, what formats do you provide?
07:00 Sasha: JSON line events, and batched parquet for analytics. also can stream to your Kafka/Splunk endpoint via secured connectivity.
07:12 Diego: That helps. one last question — do you have a sample SCIM mapping for nested groups? our IdP has nested org groups.
07:20 Sasha: Nested groups are supported by our SCIM sync if the IdP flattens groups in the SCIM payload; otherwise we'll provide a script to normalize groups during provisioning.
07:32 Jordan: Ok wrapping up: reiterate action items and owners. expect the security packet and SOC2 from me by 1/14, SCIM mapping example from Sasha by 1/13, customer to share IdP metadata and attributes by 1/12. schedule POC for next week if that works.
07:50 Anita: yes we'll prioritize and send the metadata. thanks everyone.
07:54 Jordan: Thanks all, bye.
questions: Can Redwood support EU-only data residency for a subset of workloads?
Does Redwood support BYOK/HSM integration for hosted and private deployments?
What audit log retention and export formats are available?
Can temporary role elevation (JIT) be enforced via TTL?
